words.gloss: on various things eaten and drunk (Vividhāśitapītīya)

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम विविधाशितपीतीय अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on various things eaten and drunk (Vividhāśitapītīya).
notes: Prose line (typed as 'verse'). Vividhāśitapītīya is a derived chapter name in -īya and is not split.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus said the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula (typed as 'verse').

words.gloss: whose strength is kindled by the inner fire
words.gram: m. inst. sg., bahuvrīhi (ppp. sam-√dhukṣ), with ūṣmaṇā
n. nom. sg., pres. pass. part. vi-√pac

words.gloss: in which the transformation (pāka) of all dhātus is unceasing
words.gram: n. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi, with śarīram (pākam for printed pakam)

words.gloss: whose heat of all dhātus, Vāta (māruta) and channels are unimpaired
words.gram: n. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi (dvandva inside), with śarīram (ūṣma for printed ūṇsma)

words.gloss: with increase of body (upacaya), strength, complexion, happiness and life-span

hindi: विविध प्रकार का खाया, पिया, चाटा और चबाया गया, प्राणी के लिए हितकर (आहार), भीतरी अग्नि से प्रदीप्त बल वाली अपनी-अपनी ऊष्मा से भली-भाँति पचता हुआ, समय पर, जिसमें सभी धातुओं का पाक निरन्तर होता रहता है और जिसकी सभी धातुओं की ऊष्मा, मारुत तथा स्रोत अक्षत हैं, ऐसे सम्पूर्ण शरीर को उपचय, बल, वर्ण, सुख और आयु से युक्त करता है और शरीर की धातुओं को ऊर्जा देता है।
english: (Food) of various kinds, eaten, drunk, licked and chewed, wholesome for a person, being properly digested by its own respective heat (ūṣman), whose strength is kindled by the inner fire, at the proper time endows the whole body, in which the transformation (pāka) of all the dhātus is unceasing and in which the heat of all the dhātus, Vāta (māruta) and the channels are unimpaired, with increase of body (upacaya), strength, complexion, happiness and life-span, and invigorates the dhātus of the body.

text_flags.why: possible: -dhātupakam gives no word; -pākam 'transformation, digestion' (√pac) fits the sense, cf. vipacyamānaṃ in the same unit
'ṇs' is not a possible Sanskrit sequence; ūṣma- 'heat' (as ūṣmaṇā in the same unit) is meant
śrīram makes no sense as the object here; śarīra is printed in the same line (śarīradhātūn)

notes: Prose line (typed as 'verse'). The two accusative bahuvrīhis (-pākam, -srotaḥ) are taken with śarīram; 'food' is understood as the subject. kālavat may also be taken with vipacyamānam ('being digested in due time'). anavasthita literally 'not standing still', rendered 'unceasing'.

hindi: क्योंकि धातुएँ, जिनका आहार धातुएँ हैं, अपनी प्रकृति का अनुसरण करती हैं।
english: For the dhātus, having dhātus as their food, maintain their normal state.
notes: dhātvāhārāḥ may also mean 'whose food is the elements' (dhātu of the food); the literal 'having dhātus as food' is kept.

hindi: वहाँ आहार का प्रसाद नामक रस और मल नामक किट्ट उत्पन्न होता है।
english: There, the rasa called the essence (prasāda) of food and the residue (kiṭṭa) called waste (mala) are produced.
notes: Prose line (typed as 'verse'). The verb abhinirvartate is singular with two subjects (rasaḥ, kiṭṭam); kept as printed.

words.gloss: sweat, urine, faeces, Vāta, Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman)
wastes of ears, eyes, nose, mouth, hair-pores and genitals
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: head hair, beard, body hair, nails and the like

hindi: किट्ट से स्वेद, मूत्र, पुरीष, वात, पित्त और श्लेष्मा; कान, आँख, नाक, मुख, रोमकूप और जननेन्द्रिय के मल; और केश, दाढ़ी-मूँछ, रोम, नख आदि अवयव पुष्ट होते हैं।
english: From the residue are nourished sweat, urine, faeces, Vāta, Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman), the wastes of the ears, eyes, nose, mouth, hair-pores and genitals, and parts such as head hair, beard, body hair and nails.
notes: Vāta, Pitta and Kapha are here listed among the products of the residue (kiṭṭa); rendered with the doṣa names as printed. puṣyanti (class 4) is rendered 'are nourished' (intransitive 'thrive').

words.gloss: rasa, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen and ojas
the substances of the five senses
called the essence of the dhātus
the body's joints, ligaments, slimy fluid (picchā) and the like

hindi: परन्तु आहार-रस से रस, रुधिर, मांस, मेद, अस्थि, मज्जा, शुक्र और ओज, पाँचों इन्द्रियों के द्रव्य, जो धातु-प्रसाद कहलाते हैं, तथा शरीर की सन्धियाँ, बन्धन, पिच्छा आदि अवयव पुष्ट होते हैं।
english: But from the rasa of food are nourished rasa, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen and ojas (vital essence), and the substances of the five senses, which are called the essence of the dhātus (dhātuprasāda), and parts such as the body's joints, ligaments and slimy fluid (picchā).
notes: medo'sthi is printed medosthi without avagraha. bandha 'binding' is rendered 'ligaments'. dhātuprasādasaṃjñakāni may qualify the whole list or only the items before it; taken with the whole preceding list.

hindi: वे सभी धातुएँ ही, मल नामक और प्रसाद नामक, रस और मल से पुष्ट होती हुई, आयु और शरीर के अनुसार अपने परिमाण का अनुसरण करती हैं।
english: All these dhātus indeed, those called waste and those called essence, being nourished by rasa and waste, keep to their own measure according to age and body.
notes: sarva eva = sarve eva (e > a before a vowel).

words.gram: m. nom. du., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ava-√sthā

hindi: इस प्रकार अपने परिमाण में स्थित रस और मल, सम धातुओं वाले आश्रय की धातु-साम्यता को बनाए रखते हैं।
english: Thus rasa and waste, remaining in their own measure, maintain the balance of the dhātus of their support (āśraya), which has balanced dhātus.
notes: āśraya 'support' is the body that houses them.

hindi: परन्तु किसी कारण से क्षीण या बढ़ी हुई प्रसाद नामक धातुओं की, आहार-मूलक वृद्धि और क्षय के द्वारा, रस आरोग्य के लिए साम्यता उत्पन्न करता है; और किट्ट मलों की ठीक इसी प्रकार।
english: But when the dhātus called essence have become depleted or increased from some cause, the rasa produces their balance for health by increase and decrease rooted in food; and the residue just so for the wastes.
notes: vṛddhikṣayābhyām pairs with kṣīṇavṛddhānām in order: increase for the depleted, decrease for the increased. The last clause is elliptical (verb and object of the first clause understood).

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ati-√ric

words.gloss: with qualities of cold and heat in alternation
words.gram: m. inst. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
m. nom. pl., pres. pass. part. upa-√car

words.gloss: bringing about balance of the body's dhātus

hindi: अपने परिमाण से अधिक हुए मल तो, निकाले जाते हुए और शीत-उष्ण के पर्याय वाले गुणों से उपचारित होते हुए, शरीर की धातुओं की साम्यता करने वाले पाए जाते हैं।
english: Wastes exceeding their own measure, however, being eliminated and being treated with qualities of cold and heat in alternation, are found to bring about balance of the body's dhātus.

text_flags.why: ud + √sṛj gives utsarga/utsargin; 'utasarg-' is not a possible form (an extra a)

notes: paryāya 'alternation, reversal' may mean that the opposite quality is applied (cold for hot and hot for cold); the literal 'in alternation' is kept. utsargin literally 'having discharge'.

hindi: उन मल और प्रसाद नामक धातुओं के स्रोत तो उनके गमन के मुख हैं।
english: Now, the channels (srotas) are the gateways of passage of these dhātus called waste and essence.
notes: Prose line (typed as 'verse'). Nominal sentence, copula understood. ayanamukha may also be read as a dvandva 'pathways and openings'.

hindi: वे विभाग के अनुसार अपनी-अपनी धातुओं को भरते हैं।
english: They fill the dhātus according to division, each its own.
notes: yathāvibhāgena: each channel according to its share; rendered literally.

words.gloss: arising from what is eaten, drunk, licked and chewed

hindi: इस प्रकार यह शरीर खाए, पिए, चाटे और चबाए गए (आहार) से उत्पन्न है।
english: Thus this body arises from what is eaten, drunk, licked and chewed.

words.gloss: arising from what is eaten, drunk, licked and chewed

hindi: और इस शरीर में रोग खाए, पिए, चाटे और चबाए गए (आहार) से उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: And the diseases in this body arise from what is eaten, drunk, licked and chewed.
notes: asmiñ śarīre: n before ś written ñ by sandhi.

words.gloss: the particulars of the use of the wholesome and the unwholesome
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: making the difference between good and ill

hindi: परन्तु यहाँ हितकर और अहितकर के उपयोग की विशेषताएँ शुभ और अशुभ का भेद करने वाली होती हैं।
english: But here the particulars of the use of the wholesome and the unwholesome are what make the difference between good and ill.
notes: iti closes Ātreya's statement; not translated.

words.gram: m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. sam-ā-√khyā
m. nom. pl., pres. part. ātm. upa-√yuj
m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. sam-ā-√khyā

words.gloss: consisting in the particulars of the use of the wholesome and the unwholesome
the difference between good and ill
words.gram: m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: ऐसा कहने वाले भगवान् आत्रेय से अग्निवेश ने कहा: "क्योंकि, भगवन्, हितकर कहे गए आहार का भी उपयोग करते हुए लोग रोगी भी और नीरोग भी दिखाई देते हैं, और ठीक वैसे ही अहितकर कहे गए (आहार का उपयोग करते हुए)। ऐसा देखे जाने पर हम शुभ और अशुभ के भेद को हितकर और अहितकर के उपयोग की विशेषता-रूप कैसे जानें?"
english: To the venerable Ātreya, who spoke thus, Agniveśa said: "For, venerable one, (people) using even food declared wholesome are seen to be diseased and free from disease, and just so (those using food) declared unwholesome. When this is seen, how do we find the difference between good and ill to consist in the particulars of the use of the wholesome and the unwholesome?"
notes: Prose line (typed as 'verse'). agniveśa uvāca = agniveśaḥ uvāca; upalabhāmaha iti = upalabhāmahe iti (sandhi). In Hindi 'रोगी भी और नीरोग भी' renders ca ... ca.

words.gloss: of those who use wholesome food
by the use of wholesome food
sounds, touches, forms, tastes and smells

hindi: भगवान् आत्रेय ने उससे कहा: "अग्निवेश, हितकर आहार का उपयोग करने वालों में उस (आहार) के कारण रोग उत्पन्न नहीं होते; और केवल हितकर आहार के उपयोग से ही सब रोगों का भय पार नहीं हो जाता। क्योंकि अहितकर आहार के उपयोग के बिना भी रोग के अन्य कारण हैं, जैसे: काल-विपर्यय, प्रज्ञापराध, और असात्म्य शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस और गन्ध।"
english: The venerable Ātreya said to him: "Agniveśa, in those who use wholesome food, diseases caused by that (food) do not arise; nor is the fear of all diseases overcome merely by the use of wholesome food alone. For even apart from the use of unwholesome food there are other sources of disease (rogaprakṛti), namely: the reversal of the seasons (kālaviparyaya), the offence of intellect (prajñāparādha), and unsuitable sounds, touches, forms, tastes and smells."

text_flags.why: possible: 'antā' gives no sense here; P12 resumes with 'tāś ca rogaprakṛtayo', so rogaprakṛtayaḥ is the noun and the word before it is most likely anyāḥ 'other' (anyā before r)

notes: Prose line (typed as 'verse'). tannimittāḥ 'caused by that' is taken as 'caused by that (wholesome food)'. kāla may mean time in general; rendered 'seasons' as kālaviparyaya. rasa in the sense list = taste (object of the tongue). kevalam with eva doubles the restriction; both kept ('merely ... alone').

words.gram: m. acc. sg., pres. part. ātm. upa-√yuj

hindi: और वे रोग के कारण रसों का भली-भाँति उपयोग करने वाले पुरुष को भी अशुभ से युक्त कर देते हैं; इसलिए हितकर आहार का उपयोग करने वाले भी रोगी दिखाई देते हैं।
english: And those sources of disease bring ill upon even a man who uses the tastes properly; therefore even those who use wholesome food are seen to be diseased.
notes: rasān 'tastes' may stand for foods in general. upapādayanti literally 'bring (him) together with ill'.

words.gloss: of those who use unwholesome food

hindi: अहितकर आहार का उपयोग करने वालों का अपचार तो कारणवश तुरन्त दोषयुक्त नहीं होता।
english: In those who use unwholesome food, however, the wrong use (apacāra) does not, for a reason, become harmful at once.
notes: kāraṇataḥ 'for a reason': the reasons follow in P14-P17.

hindi: क्योंकि सभी अपथ्य समान दोष वाले नहीं होते, न सभी दोष समान बल वाले होते हैं, और न सभी शरीर रोग को सहने में समर्थ होते हैं।
english: For not all unwholesome things are equally harmful, nor are all doṣas of equal strength, nor are all bodies capable of resisting disease.
notes: tulyadoṣa literally 'having equal fault (doṣa)'. vyādhikṣamatva 'capacity to withstand disease'.

words.gloss: through place, time, combination, potency (vīrya) and excess of quantity

hindi: क्योंकि वही अपथ्य देश, काल, संयोग, वीर्य और प्रमाण के अतियोग से और अधिक अपथ्य हो जाता है।
english: For the same unwholesome thing becomes still more unwholesome through place, time, combination, potency (vīrya) and excess of quantity.

text_flags.why: 'apathayṃ' is not a word; the same line has apathyaṃ (tadeva hyapathyaṃ)

notes: atiyoga 'excess' may attach to pramāṇa alone ('excessive quantity', as rendered) or to every member ('excess of place, time ...').

words.gloss: whose measures of treatment are opposed
arising in a seat of life (prāṇāyatana)

hindi: वही दोष, जब मिश्रित उत्पत्ति वाला, विरुद्ध उपक्रम वाला, गहराई तक पहुँचा हुआ, चिरकाल से स्थित, प्राणायतन में उत्पन्न और मर्म पर आघात करने वाला हो, तब कष्टतम और अत्यन्त शीघ्रकारी हो जाता है।
english: The same doṣa, when it is of combined origin, has opposed measures of treatment (upakrama), has gone deep, is long-standing, arises in a seat of life (prāṇāyatana) and injures vital points (marma), becomes the gravest and the most quick-acting.
notes: saṃsṛṣṭayoni 'whose source is combined' (combined with another doṣa, or of mixed causes). The 'when ... then' structure is supplied for the series of qualifying adjectives.

words.gloss: whose flesh, blood and bone are not compact

words.gram: n. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa, ppp. upa-√ci

hindi: और अत्यन्त स्थूल, अत्यन्त कृश, जिनके मांस, रक्त और अस्थि सुगठित नहीं हैं, दुर्बल, असात्म्य आहार से पुष्ट हुए, अल्प आहार वाले और अल्प सत्त्व वाले शरीर रोग को सहन न करने वाले होते हैं; इनके विपरीत शरीर तो रोग को सहन करने वाले होते हैं।
english: And bodies that are excessively obese, excessively lean, whose flesh, blood and bone are not compact, weak, built up by unsuitable food, taking little food and of little mind (sattva), are unable to withstand disease; the opposite ones, however, withstand disease.
notes: aniviṣṭa literally 'not firmly set'.

words.gloss: particulars of unwholesome food, doṣa and body
words.gram: m. abl. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: और इन्हीं अपथ्य आहार, दोष और शरीर की विशेषताओं से रोग मृदु, दारुण, शीघ्र उत्पन्न होने वाले और देर से प्रभाव करने वाले होते हैं।
english: And from these very particulars of unwholesome food, doṣa and body, diseases become mild, dreadful, quickly arising and slow-acting.
notes: cirakārin literally 'acting after a long time'.

hindi: अग्निवेश, वे ही वात, पित्त और श्लेष्मा विशेष स्थानों में कुपित होकर विशेष रोगों को उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: Those very Vāta, Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman), aggravated in particular sites, produce particular diseases, Agniveśa.
notes: ta eva = te eva (e > a before a vowel). sthānaviśeṣe is singular ('in a particular site'), rendered distributively.

hindi: वहाँ रस आदि स्थानों में कुपित दोषों के, जिस स्थान में जो-जो रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं, उन-उन का हम यथावत् क्रम से व्याख्यान करेंगे।
english: There, of the doṣas aggravated in the sites rasa and the rest, whichever diseases arise in whichever site, those we shall duly explain in order.
notes: Prose line (typed as 'verse'). rasa here is the first dhātu as a site.

hindi: अश्रद्धा, अरुचि, मुख की विरसता, रस का ज्ञान न होना, हृल्लास, भारीपन, तन्द्रा, अङ्गमर्द सहित ज्वर, तम,
english: Lack of desire (for food), loss of taste (aruci), bad taste in the mouth, inability to perceive taste, nausea (hṛllāsa), heaviness, drowsiness, fever with body-ache, darkness (tamas),
notes: SENTENCE: the list of rasa-born diseases runs through 9-10 and is closed by 'rasapradoṣajā rogāḥ' in 11a. aśraddhā literally 'lack of desire'; 'for food' supplied. tamas 'darkness' (a feeling of darkness) is kept as printed. Metre: both half-lines 16 syllables.

hindi: पाण्डुता, स्रोतों का अवरोध, क्लैब्य, साद, शरीर की कृशता, अग्नि का नाश, असमय की झुर्रियाँ और पके बाल,
english: pallor, obstruction of the channels, impotence (klaibya), lassitude, leanness of the body, loss of the digestive fire (agni), and untimely wrinkles and grey hairs,
notes: SENTENCE: continues the list of 9; closed in 11a. ayathākālāḥ qualifies valayaḥ and, by sense, palitāni. Metre: both half-lines 16 syllables.

words.gloss: born of the vitiation of rasa
those born of the vitiation of blood

hindi: (ये) रस के दोष से उत्पन्न रोग हैं। अब रक्त के दोष से उत्पन्न (रोग) कहे जाएँगे: कुष्ठ, वीसर्प, पिडकाएँ, रक्तपित्त, असृग्दर,
english: (these) are the diseases born of the vitiation of rasa. Those born of the vitiation of blood will be told: kuṣṭha, vīsarpa, eruptions (piḍakā), raktapitta, asṛgdara,
notes: SENTENCE: 11a closes the rasa list of 9-10; the blood list begins in 11b and runs to 13b ('raktapradoṣāj jāyante'). vakṣyante is taken with raktadoṣajāḥ. vīsarpa and asṛgdara kept Sanskrit. Metre: both half-lines 16 syllables.

words.gloss: inflammation (pāka) of anus, penis and mouth
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: गुदा, मेढ्र और मुख का पाक, प्लीहा, गुल्म और विद्रधि, नीलिका, कामला, व्यङ्ग, पिप्लु और तिलकालक,
english: inflammation (pāka) of the anus, penis and mouth, plīhā (spleen), gulma and vidradhi (abscess), nīlikā, kāmalā, vyaṅga, piplus and tilakālakas,
notes: SENTENCE: continues the list of blood-born diseases. The printed pipplavaḥ (double p) is kept; the disease is elsewhere called piplu (plural piplavaḥ); the metre does not decide (the syllable is heavy either way), so no flag. tilakālaka is taken as one disease name; a division into tilaka + alaka is also conceivable. plīhā is printed as the name of a disease of the spleen. Metre: both half-lines 16 syllables.

words.gloss: those born of the vitiation of flesh

hindi: दद्रु, चर्मदला, श्वित्र, पामा, कोठ और अस्रमण्डल रक्त के दोष से उत्पन्न होते हैं। अब मांस के दोष से उत्पन्न (रोगों) को सुनो:
english: dadru, carmadalā, śvitra, pāmā, koṭha and blood-circles (asramaṇḍala) arise from the vitiation of blood. Hear those born of the vitiation of flesh:
notes: SENTENCE: 13a ends the blood list begun in 11b; the flesh list follows in 14. koṭhāsramaṇḍalam is a compound of two list items; given here as koṭha + asramaṇḍalam. The printed carmadalā is taken as feminine nom. sg. asra 'blood', maṇḍala 'circle'; the literal gloss is used. Metre: both half-lines 16 syllables.

words.gloss: pūtimāṃsa (putrid flesh), alajī, gaṇḍa, gaṇḍamālā and upajihvikā

hindi: अधिमांस, अर्बुद, कील, गलशालूक और गलशुण्डिका, पूतिमांस, अलजी, गण्ड, गण्डमाला और उपजिह्विका,
english: adhimāṃsa (excess flesh), arbuda, kīla, galaśālūka and galaśuṇḍikā, pūtimāṃsa (putrid flesh), alajī, gaṇḍa, gaṇḍamālā and upajihvikā,
notes: SENTENCE: the flesh list runs into 15a ('vidyān māṃsāśrayān'). adhimāṃsārbudaṃ is a compound of two list items, given as adhimāṃsa + arbudam. galaśālūkaśuṇḍike: gala 'throat' is taken with both members (galaśālūka, galaśuṇḍikā). All names kept Sanskrit; literal glosses only. Metre: both half-lines 16 syllables.

hindi: इन्हें मांस पर आश्रित जानना चाहिए। मेद पर आश्रित (रोगों) को तो हम बताते हैं: निन्दित (अवस्थाएँ) और प्रमेहों के जो पूर्वरूप हैं।
english: One should know (these) as based in flesh. Those based in fat we declare: the condemned (conditions), and those which are the prodromal signs of the pramehas.
notes: ninditāni 'the condemned (ones)' is translated literally; its referent is not stated in this chunk. 'conditions' / 'अवस्थाएँ' is supplied. The relative yāni ... ca has no correlative in the unit. Metre: both half-lines 16 syllables.
